messages:
marta: hi all, marta here (joined today). I can `kubectl get pods -n infra-tools` after switching to `redwood-dev`, but `kubectl port-forward svc/prometheus 9090:9090 -n infra-tools` fails with `error: pods "prometheus-..." is forbidden: User \"marta@redwood.ai\" cannot create resource \"pods/portforward\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"infra-tools\"`.

jen (devex): welcome @marta! :wave: port-forward is commonly blocked by default for new hires. pinging @devops-ian to confirm the usual flow (temp role vs group).

devops-ian: hey @marta, welcome. TL;DR: you have view on pods but not the pod/portforward subresource. We can either (A) grant a short-lived Role that allows `create` on `pods/portforward` + `get` on pods in infra-tools, or (B) add your SSO account to `infra-operators` group for longer-term access if you need it regularly. Which do you prefer?

marta: short-lived for now please, I only need to port-forward for a pairing session this afternoon.

ops-bot: INFRA-1401 created by devops-ian: "temp port-forward rolebinding for marta in infra-tools". ETA: 15m.

devops-ian: i'll apply a Role + RoleBinding scoped to `infra-tools`. YAML i'm about to apply (preview):

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: onboarding-portforward-marta
  namespace: infra-tools
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods/portforward"]
  verbs: ["create"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: onboarding-portforward-marta-binding
  namespace: infra-tools
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: "marta@redwood.ai"
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: onboarding-portforward-marta
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

This will be temporary (24h). After that, if you need persistent access we'll move you to the infra-operators SSO group.

marta: thanks! Quick Q: earlier `kubectl auth can-i port-forward pods -n infra-tools` returned `yes` but the command still failed. Is `kubectl auth can-i` reliable for subresources?

devops-ian: good catch. `kubectl auth can-i` checks the current token and impersonation args; sometimes people run it without `--as` which can be misleading. Also some auth providers cache tokens and `kubectl` may be using a cached credential for list/get but not for portforward. Best to run `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n infra-tools --as marta@redwood.ai` to mirror the operation. If that returns yes and port-forward still fails, paste the exact error and we'll look at audit logs.

jen (devex): small onboarding tip for future hires: add a tiny function in your shell to switch contexts quickly, e.g. `krd() { kubectl config use-context redwood-$1; }` then `krd dev`. saved me a bunch of time on day 1 :slightly_smiling_face:. also doc link: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/k8s-quicktips (has port-forward troubleshooting).

ops-bot: INFRA-1401 status: applied by devops-ian.

devops-ian: applied. try your port-forward again. If you still see forbidden, do `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n infra-tools --as marta@redwood.ai` and paste output.

marta: re-ran the command and now port-forward works! thanks so much.

arman (platform): FYI team, we're thinking about changing the default new-hire profile so devs get a time-limited port-forward capability for non-prod namespaces to reduce support tickets. cc @jen (devex) for onboarding checklist change.

jen (devex): noted, i'll add that to the onboarding improvements doc. Also adding a note about verifying `kubectl config view --raw` when folks report weird token issues.

marta: everything I need for the session works. Appreciate the quick response everyone :tada:
